title: Trust the numbers: Germans are open to a more hawkish China policy – European Council on Foreign Relations
gist: ECFR polling across 15 European countries finds Germans the most China-sceptical public in Europe — 60% of CDU and SPD supporters call China an adversary or rival — while Italian and Spanish publics still see China as a partner or ally (56% and 65%). With German manufacturing down roughly 420,000 jobs since 2019 and still shedding 10,000 a month, the authors argue Berlin's restraint on China trade defence is elite reluctance without a voter constraint, and that pairing electrification with de-risking is the politically rewarded package.

themes.theme: The polling gap between German elites and voters

insights.claim: Germans are the most China-sceptical public of 15 European countries surveyed by ECFR, with 60% of Christian Democrat and Social Democrat supporters regarding China as an adversary or rival.
insights.speaker: Nele Anders, Nina Schmelzer
insights.so_what: The domestic political constraint on German China hawkishness is imaginary — policy can shift faster than corporate lobbying assumes.
insights.quote: ECFR polling data find that Germans are the most China-sceptical out of 15 European countries surveyed.
insights.locator: Yet, one thing Berlin should not worry about

insights.claim: Southern European publics run the opposite way, with 56% in Italy and 65% in Spain still viewing China as a necessary partner or even an ally, while the French public sits closest to the sceptical Germans.
insights.speaker: Nele Anders, Nina Schmelzer
insights.so_what: EU-wide China measures will face public-opinion resistance in Italy and Spain even where their governments push for trade defence — a source of implementation slippage.
insights.quote: In Italy and Spain, 56% and 65% of people hold this view respectively.

insights.claim: Macron's increasingly hawkish posture toward Beijing appears to have found a receptive French audience, making France the second-most China-sceptical public after Germany.
insights.speaker: Nele Anders, Nina Schmelzer
insights.so_what: Franco-German alignment on China hawkishness now has a public-opinion floor under it, raising the odds tougher EU measures survive political cycles.
insights.quote: President Emmanuel Macron’s increasingly hawkish political posture vis-à-vis Beijing may have found an audience willing to listen

themes.theme: German industrial damage from the China shock

insights.claim: German manufacturing lost around 420,000 jobs between 2019 and 2025 and continues to shed 10,000 jobs each month.
insights.speaker: Nele Anders, Nina Schmelzer
insights.so_what: A run-rate of 120k manufacturing job losses a year is a hard political clock on German industrial policy — expect escalating intervention, not patience.
insights.quote: its manufacturing sector lost around 420,000 jobs between 2019 and 2025 and it continues to shed 10,000 jobs each month
insights.locator: The China shock has hit Germany particularly hard

insights.claim: The German car industry is bearing the highest cost of the China shock, being squeezed out of a market increasingly dominated by Chinese manufacturers both at home and abroad.
insights.speaker: Nele Anders, Nina Schmelzer
insights.so_what: German autos are the sector where domestic political pain and trade-defence advocacy will converge first — the constituency for tariffs is now inside the industry.
insights.quote: The car industry is paying the highest costs, being squeezed out of a market increasingly dominated by Chinese manufacturers at home and abroad.
insights.locator: The China shock has hit Germany

insights.claim: When France, Italy, Lithuania, the Netherlands and Spain recently pressed the European Commission for tougher and faster trade defence action against China, Germany not only declined to join but called for stronger industrial ties with Beijing.
insights.speaker: Nele Anders, Nina Schmelzer
insights.so_what: The five-country bloc pushing trade defence is the coalition to track; German accession to it is the switch that unlocks EU-level action.

insights.claim: At their June 2026 meeting EU leaders backed a stronger trade defence toolbox against China including the Industrial Accelerator Act's 'Buy European' provisions and limits on high-risk Chinese technology, with Germany cautiously supportive rather than acting as a spoiler.
insights.speaker: Nele Anders, Nina Schmelzer
insights.so_what: 'Buy European' procurement rules plus Chinese-tech restrictions are now live EU policy with German assent — a direct revenue risk for Chinese suppliers into EU public and infrastructure demand.
insights.quote: This included instruments such as the Industrial Accelerator Act’s “Buy European” provisions and limits on high-risk Chinese technology.
insights.locator: The mood in the European Council is shifting

insights.claim: The combination of rising public scepticism, industrial pain and European-level appetite for assertiveness creates an unused political mandate that German decision-makers could still seize.
insights.speaker: Nele Anders, Nina Schmelzer
insights.so_what: Positioning should assume German China policy has more upside hawkishness priced out than in — the gap between elite caution and mandate is the trade.
insights.locator: Nevertheless, the combination of growing public scepticism

themes.theme: Electrification and de-risking as one package

insights.claim: 57% of German voters back investment in renewables amounting to growing electrification of the economy, and 61% across all ECFR-polled countries support prioritising renewables and the clean tech sector.
insights.speaker: Nele Anders, Nina Schmelzer
insights.so_what: Public support for electrification is broad and stable across Europe, underpinning demand-side policy for grids, wind and batteries even amid a green-policy backlash narrative.
insights.quote: Across the countries polled by ECFR, 61% of respondents say they support prioritising renewables and the clean tech sector.
insights.locator: The German public’s views on the energy transition

insights.claim: Governments can accelerate the energy transition while simultaneously de-risking clean tech by supporting domestic European industries from wind to batteries, limiting emerging dependencies on China.
insights.speaker: Nele Anders, Nina Schmelzer
insights.so_what: European wind and battery manufacturers are the designated policy beneficiaries of coupling decarbonisation to de-risking — a subsidy and protection tailwind.
insights.locator: This public support should help persuade leaders

insights.claim: Delay is the riskier course because Chinese economic policy is already doing irreparable damage to European industry, and governments that fail to protect an increasingly electrified economy from Chinese weaponisation will pay at the ballot box.
insights.speaker: Nele Anders, Nina Schmelzer
insights.so_what: Electoral punishment as the stated mechanism means European China policy ratchets one way — assume tightening, not reversion, across the cycle.
insights.quote: Those that pursue electrification and economic de-risking as a single package are most likely to reap the political rewards.
insights.locator: For Berlin, and capitals across Europe
